headline: Google Photos lets you turn off Shimmer feature after user complaints
summary: The AI-powered sparkle effect that outlines people and objects can now be disabled via settings, with Google Photos rolling out the option in its latest update.
details: Google Photos has introduced a toggle to disable the 'Shimmer' feature, which adds a temporary sparkly outline to subjects in photos. Users had complained about the AI-driven effect since its introduction earlier this year, citing annoyance and even motion sickness.
The 'Show shimmer' toggle can be found in Settings > Preferences within the Google Photos app. It is enabled by default, so users can simply switch it off to stop the effect from appearing.

Alongside the Shimmer control, Google Photos is also rolling out an update that allows users to directly use their phone's camera when selecting photos for AI features like Remix and Photo. This aims to streamline the process for quick edits.
Google stated that this integration is designed for features requiring quick, temporary input, such as simple photos or funny faces, making it easier to access the 'magic' of AI editing on the go.

headline: US bans foreign-made advanced robots and power inverters over security risks
summary: The FCC cites 'unacceptable risks to national security' as it targets devices capable of locomotion and perception, impacting China's growing robotics industry.
details: The US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) has announced a ban on the import of "advanced robotic devices" and power inverters manufactured in foreign countries, citing national security concerns. This move is expected to significantly impact China's burgeoning robotics sector, which has seen viral videos of humanoid robots performing various tasks.

The ban specifically targets 'mobile' robots, including humanoid and quadruped models, that are capable of locomotion, obstacle avoidance, navigation, and possess environmental perception sensors along with network connectivity. The devices must also weigh over 4.4 pounds to be included in the ban.

While the FCC states the ban is not country-specific, it will disproportionately affect China, a leading producer of these advanced robots and power inverters used in renewable energy systems. Companies like Sungrow and Huawei are among the major power inverter producers based in China.

The FCC justifies the ban by citing "unacceptable risks to the national security of the United States or the safety and security of United States persons." The definition of an 'advanced robotic device' could even include future robot vacuums if they meet the specified criteria.

Companies wishing to import these devices can apply for a waiver, but the process does not mandate security improvements for the robots or inverters. Existing products already in the US are not affected by this ban. Manufacturers seeking waivers will need to present a plan for manufacturing their products within the United States.

Security and compatibility updates for affected robots and power inverters will be permitted until January 1st, 2029, through an additional waiver. However, the FCC's claims about how these updates are managed are being questioned, as companies are not currently required to report security updates to the agency.
